chunks: My father (peace be upon him) and the group of my scholars (peace be upon him) narrated to me from Sa'd ibn 'Abdillah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from some of our companions, from Aban, from 'Abd al-Malik al-Khath'ami, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

He said to me: O 'Abd al-Malik! Do not neglect the Ziyarah of al-Husayn ibn 'Ali (peace be upon him) and order your companions to do so. Allah will prolong your life, increase your sustenance, Allah will make you live a blissful life, and you will not die except blissfully [as a martyr], and Allah will register you among the blissful ones.

key_terms.زِيَارَة: Visitation (specifically to the shrines of Imams or prophets)

ai.seo_question: What are the spiritual and worldly benefits of visiting Imam al-Husayn (peace be upon him) according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In Kamil al-Ziyarat, Ibn Qulawayh records Imam al-Sadiq’s (a.s.) specific promise to 'Abd al-Malik al-Khath'ami that consistent Ziyarah of Imam al-Husayn (a.s.) serves as a means for divine prolongation of life (tawil al-'umr) and increased sustenance (rizq). This tradition underscores the Shia theological view that physical visitation is not merely commemorative but a spiritual conduit for tangible blessings, linking the martyr's status to the believer's ultimate success (sa'adah) in both life and death.

en.sayyid-mohsen-al-husayni-al-milani: 5. My father and all of my scholars narrated to me from Sa’d ibn ‘Abdillāh, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ‘Isā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥamamd ibn Abī Nasr, from some of our companions, from Abān, from ‘Abdil Malik Al-Khath’ami, who said:

Abū ‘Abdillāh (Imam Sādiq (a.s.)) said to me: O ‘Abd Al-Malik! Do not neglect going to the Ziyārah of Ḥusain ibn ‘Ali (a.s.) and order your friends to go to his Ziyārah, (because by going to his Ziyārah) Allāh will prolong your life, increase your sustenance, allow you to live a life of bliss and die a blissful death, as well as register you among the blissful ones.
